name: StackEval
description: A coding assistance benchmark built from real Stack Overflow questions, plus StackUnseen — a post-training-cutoff component covering emerging technologies — to test generalization beyond memorized content. Includes the first comprehensive study on LLMs-as-judges for coding tasks, examining self-preference bias and cross-model evaluation reliability. Tests real-world programming assistance scenarios across diverse languages and frameworks.
evaluation_method: accuracy; LLM-as-judge evaluation (with self-preference bias analysis)
typical_sota_score: ~60–75% on StackUnseen (frontier models; lower than main StackEval due to knowledge cutoff)
reputation: Published at NeurIPS 2024; addresses data leakage with post-cutoff StackUnseen component; includes methodological contribution on LLM-judge bias in coding evaluation
notes: NeurIPS 2024. StackUnseen (questions about technologies released after model training cutoffs) provides contamination-free evaluation. LLM-as-judge analysis reveals significant self-preference bias: models tend to rate their own outputs higher than outputs from other models. First systematic study of this bias in coding-specific evaluation. Real Stack Overflow questions ensure ecological validity.
